provider: Trystero (WebRTC signalling over BitTorrent / Nostr / MQTT / IPFS / Supabase / Firebase)
category: relay/P2P — pure SIGNALLING, zero relayed bytes

free_tier.stated: No storage and no relayed bandwidth: Trystero borrows an existing decentralised network purely to exchange WebRTC SDP offers.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Data flows peer-to-peer via WebRTC; the signalling network never sees the payload. The operator's cost is SDP messages only.

chaining: The cleanest signalling example: because only SDP crosses the third party, there is no bandwidth quota to hit and no operator who could impose one. Note the caveat that WebRTC needs a TURN relay when both peers are behind symmetric NAT. That is where real relaying cost reappears, and Trystero does not supply it.
limits_note: Signalling only. Browser WebRTC connection-count limits force a room/namespace design.
reliability_note: No TURN service included; symmetric-NAT pairs will fail to connect rather than fall back.
confidence_note: mechanically converted from the seed corpus; no page was read for this record in the storage-dossier pass. One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: 'To establish a direct peer-to-peer connection with WebRTC, a signalling channel is needed to exchange peer information (SDP). Typically this involves running your own matchmaking server but Trystero abstracts this away'; strategies listed: BitTorrent, Nostr, MQTT, Supabase, Firebase, IPFS, self-hosted WebSocket relay
'Use our free cloud server or host your own PeerServer' (free signalling broker; relayed data still needs a TURN server)

extras.agent_focus: Systematic sweep of self-hosted academic repository software (Dataverse, DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, Fedora/Islandora) scored on the four client questions: institutional-email requirement, per-file cap, per-collection/dataset cap, and whether the install enforces a quota object at all. Primary method was machine probing, not page reading: /api/info/version and /api/dataverses/:root/storage/quota?showInherited=true against the full official Dataverse installation registry (150 hostnames), the native-signup form probe /dataverseuser.xhtml?editMode=CREATE against all 83 no-quota hosts, and the platform source defaults read out of the upstream config files for DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, libp2p and iroh. Secondary coverage of the relay/P2P half of the slot.
